sentence: This project studies whether double-stranded RNA released from damaged mitochondria starts inflammation in the aging brain and in Alzheimer's disease.
This project provides molecular cloning and viral vector production, and builds gene expression plasmids and cell lines for researchers studying many diseases.
This project studies how neural stem cells take up and use glucose to control cell fate decisions during brain development.
This project builds a center that screens many genes linked to neurodevelopmental and psychiatric disorders at once to learn what those genes do.
This project studies how the interactions behind Ewing sarcoma affect transcription and DNA repair, looking at their structural basis.
This project builds a hardware and software platform that lowers the cost, time and risk of developing implantable neurotechnology devices.
This project supports research in genetics, as applied to basic biological processes and human health.
This project studies how a pro-inflammatory molecule called lysophosphatidylinositol activates the endothelium, which lines blood vessels.
This project combines imaging, genomic and longitudinal data with deep learning to predict which cervical cancer patients will fail radiation therapy.
This project studies the structures and functions of antibodies against IgE and its receptors, and how the receptor CD23 interacts with IgE.
This project tries to find out the molecular reasons prostate cancer cells change lineage and become resistant to therapy.
This project studies how Giardia parasites change into resistant cysts, a process called encystation, in which they detach from the host intestine.
This project identifies mRNA isoforms that differ in Alzheimer's disease using long-read data from human brain tissue and then develops RNA therapeutics to modulate them.
This project studies how a protease called ADAMTS9 cuts a protein called TMEM67 and how that affects kidney development and cystic kidney disease.
This project builds wearable sensors that use optical biomarkers to measure immune activity in the skin of patients with inflammatory skin diseases.
This project studies the neural circuits and signaling pathways of the locus coeruleus in the mammalian brain to understand anxiety and other affective disorders.
This project uses blood samples and quantitative proteomics to define biomarker signatures that track the course of Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
This project tests whether a home-based mHealth intervention helps young children meet guidelines for physical activity, sleep and screen-time.
This project uses machine learning on clinical and molecular data to find predictors of how patients with severe community-acquired pneumonia do over time.
This project studies how dopamine neurons in the rat mesolimbic pathway shape reward, cocaine use and substance use disorder.
